newsitem.title: GERMANY: Daimler seeks 1.3 bln DM for Cap Gemini.
newsitem.headline: Daimler seeks 1.3 bln DM for Cap Gemini.

text.p: Daimler-Benz AG subsidiary Debis said on Thursday it intends to recover its entire 1.3 billion mark ($753.4 million) investment in French software maker Cap Gemini by selling its 24.4 percent stake.
Debis's sales in the first five months of 1997 were up 25 percent from the year-earlier period, chief executive Klaus Mangold told reporters.
Mangold said Debis originally invested 1.1 billion marks in Cap Gemini in 1991, and later made a 170 million mark capital injection.
Daimler said on Wednesday it intended to spin off its stake in Cap Gemini in the medium term by issuing a convertible bond.
For the full year 1997, Mangold said he sees sales rising 400 million marks to about 2.8 billion marks. This will not be affected by the planned sale of the Cap Gemini stake, he said.
Mangold also said Debis unit Debis Systemhaus GmbH had boosted its sales 28 percent in the five-month period.
After the sale of Cap Gemini, Debis Systemhaus will continue to boost foreign sales of services for the information technology industry, he said.

Its foreign sales should rise about 50 percent to 450 million marks this year, he said. Over the long term, Systemhaus aims to boost foreign sales to 50 percent of total sales, he said. A current figure was not immediately available.
